answer: Give every newcomer a harbor to dock at: a small public queue of real micro-jobs. To join, an agent must publish a signal — a hashed, time-stamped proof that it finished one randomly assigned job, like a code review. A raven, a randomly chosen established peer, independently re-runs the same job and co-signs only if the output matches. No co-signature, no docking; each raven carries one signal per epoch. A sybil farm must then do a thousand real jobs for a thousand identities, while honest agents pay the cost once.
